MX17 at LNL · the lithium target · 22 Oct 2026

LNL ran LiF at the 18.15 MeV resonance, where fluorine makes 2.5–3.5 thousand e⁺e⁻ pairs for every ⁸Be pair. For MX17 the target is a solved problem: no fluorine, keep it cool, and the 3D fit shrugs off a drifting target.

Measured ¹⁹F and ⁷Li cross sections, a heat model of the target foils checked against ATOMKI and Hanoi, and the MX17 Geant4 tables and 3D fit for every failure mode.

1

Details

Pierfrancesco's question: the LNL ⁸Be pair spectrometer took ~790 h of beam on AN2000 in 2023–24 and has published nothing. Was it the lithium target, and would it hit us? This note answers both from public sources and our own simulation. It cannot know what LNL actually saw: the inference about their run needs confirming with them.

Hover dotted terms and data points for definitions and values. Write-up: lnl/target/TARGET_STUDY.md.

A lithium target is a micron of film on a foil, and every group that ran one at 18 MeV hit a problem

Beam left to right. Hover the layers; the table is each group’s target and what they reported.

grouptarget at the 18 MeV energieswhat went wrong (their words or ours)
ATOMKI 2016Li metal → “Li₂O”, 10 µm Al strip, Plexiglas rodsLi diffused into the Al: target “10 µm” thick, beam reached 441 keV
Hanoi 2024LiF 30 / Al 10 µm (≤ 0.8 MeV); Li₂O on 1 µm Ni“burned out (punctured) many times”; F E0 pairs “would overload” at 1.04
MEG II 2023LiPON 7 µm on 25 µm Cu25 % H₂⁺ beam put most data on 441 keV
LNL 2023–24LiF 34–935 µg/cm² at 1.03 MeVno result published; backing unknown

2

Details

The physics wants ⁷Li atoms at one proton energy (1.03–1.10 MeV for the 18.15 MeV state), so the film must be thin (≲ 300 µg/cm², ≲ 60 keV of energy loss) and stay where it was put. Everything else in the stack is a source of other γ-rays and pairs, of heat, and of scattering for the leptons.

Sources: Sas 2022 (arXiv:2205.07744) §V for ATOMKI 2016; Tran The Anh 2024 (arXiv:2401.11676) for Hanoi; MEG II EPJC 85, 763; Góngora-Servín 2025 (APPB Supp 18 2-A13) for LNL. The Hanoi spectrometer was built with ATOMKI.

At 441 keV the ⁷Li resonance wins: LiF is a fine calibration target.

Above 0.8 MeV the order flips. At 1.03 MeV each F nucleus makes ×2,282 more pairs than each Li nucleus.

ATOMKI/Hanoi: the E0 pairs “would overload our electronics” there. LNL ran LiF at 1.03 MeV.

3

Details

The 6.05 MeV first excited state of ¹⁶O is 0⁺, like the ground state, so it can only decay by internal pair creation (E0): every ¹⁹F(p,α_π) reaction makes a pair, with 5.0 MeV of kinetic energy shared between the leptons. The 6.13/6.92/7.12 MeV lines are real γ-rays that convert, Compton-scatter and pile up.

α_π: digitised from L. Redigolo et al., J. Phys. G 51 (2024) 075106 Figs 6 and 8 (E_cm 1.04–1.25 MeV data; R-matrix to 1.0 MeV); below that a constant-S extrapolation, an upper-side estimate (±×3). αγ: TUNL compilation (2021PH03, 90° × 4π, isotropic ±30 %; ×1.6 for the 6.92/7.12 lines, ×2 uncertain). ¹¹B: Breit-Wigner of the 17.23 MeV 1⁻ level of ¹²C with (2J+1)Γγ₀ ≥ 115 eV (Kelley 2017), Γp/Γ = 0.5 assumed: ~7 µb at 1.03 MeV against ⁷Li(p,γ₀) 33 µb.

Table: lnl/out/target/cross_sections.csv; code lnl/target/target_model.py.

4

Details

Integrated through each target with PSTAR stopping (Bragg additivity), the Zahnow ⁷Li cross sections and the ¹⁹F cross sections of the previous slide. LNL’s “1.03 MeV at the centre” for the 935 µg/cm² target means ~1.12 MeV in, ~0.93 out (190 keV of loss): the upper half sits where α_π rises to 3–7 mb.

The ratio counts every pair in 4π. A detector then cuts on energy: one E0 pair has 5.0 MeV, an 18 MeV IPC pair 17 MeV. What fluorine costs is rate, dead time and pile-up (next two slides), not a fake 18 MeV pair from a single reaction.

lnl/out/target/scenarios.csv, fluorine_scan.csv (thickness × energy grid).

In an LNL-like clover array the fluorine pairs outrun the ⁸Be pairs by thousands

A toy of the LNL 2023 geometry: 4 clovers, 10×10 cm at 12.75 cm, ΔE–E triple coincidence; 0.8 µA

¹⁹F E0 pairs

⁸Be IPC pairs

Thick LiF at 1.03 MeV: ~8,389 triple coincidences per second in each clover, almost all fluorine.

The ⁸Be pairs: 31,328/day thick, 1,226/day thin, before any cut.

A cut on energy removes single E0 pairs; the DAQ still has to take them, and they pile up.

TOY (×2). Triple coincidence and acceptances from Góngora-Servín 2025 and Marchi 2021

5

Details

A toy, to ×2: 4 clovers, each 4.9 % of 4π; a lepton above 1 MeV passes the triple coincidence; a 6–7 MeV γ does so with 6×10⁻⁴ per clover hit (Marchi 2021, slide 14) and leaves something in an E block 30 % of the time. Two-clover acceptance 1.2 % for 18 MeV IPC (Marchi 2021, slide 20); for the wide-angle E0 pairs 3 % × 0.64 (both leptons above 1 MeV).

Thick target at 0.8 µA: ¹⁹F pairs 1.1e+05/s and γ 3.6e+05/s into 4π; each clover sees 13,667 hits/s, a 1.4e-03 chance of a second hit in 100 ns. ⁸Be IPC pairs into 4π: 30.2/s.

Not in the toy and possibly worse: if the telescopes sit in the vacuum without an absorber, ¹⁹F(p,α₀) α (~7 MeV), ⁷Li(p,α)α (8.7 MeV) and backscattered protons reach the ΔE bars, ~10⁵ α/s into 4π on the thick target. (ask)

6

Details

Per E0 pair (as built): a leg in a given arm 2.0 %, in any arm 8.3 %, in two arms never (0 in 10⁶); a drift-gap track per arm 28 %. Per ¹⁹F γ: a leg 0.08 % per arm. A ¹⁹F leg carries at most ~6.9 MeV, so an accidental two-arm event needs two γ legs (or three hits) to reach the 13–18 MeV window.

Model: legs/arm = ¹⁹F + ⁸Be (0.39 %/4 per γ) + 15/s cosmics; two-arm accidentals 6 × 20 ns × R²; the pair trigger (~22/s × I) never prescaled; DREAM 298 µs non-paralysable; the singles prescale P is the smallest power of 2 that keeps ≥ 90 % live. MM window 20 × 60 ns. TOF keeps 0.6/20 of accidentals (0.3 ns cut in a 20 ns window). Accidental pile-up: leg energies drawn from the Geant4 library, 100 ns integration.

lnl/target/target_rates.py → rates_mx17.csv; libraries from target/lxplus/target_singles.py over L6/L8 (E0) and L3/L8 (γ) runs.

ATOMKI 2016’s strip: 657 °C at 1 µA and 0.8 MeV. That is where Li diffuses through the Al within hours, and why Hanoi’s foils “burned out many times” at 1–1.5 µA.

thermal.csv, limits.csv · strip geometry: Gulyás 2016 (NIM A 808, 21) · emissivity is the main unknown

7

Details

Model (target_model.py temp_strip / temp_disk): finite-volume steady state, conduction in the foil to a clamp at 27 °C (a strip 5 × 50 mm held at both ends 25 mm from the beam, as Gulyás 2016; or a disk clamped at r = 10 mm), radiation from both faces (Al ε = 0.08, C 0.85, Cu 0.05), Gaussian beam σ = 1.5 mm. Power = I × energy lost in film + foil: at 1.05 MeV the beam leaves 10 µm Al at ~0.48 MeV (0.53 W/µA); at 0.8 MeV it stops in it (0.77 W/µA); graphite and Cu stop it (all of it).

Sensitivity: with ε = 0.3–0.6 the strip at 1 µA drops to 240–350 °C, and at 5 µA is still 590–800 °C; σ = 3 mm takes 10–25 % off. Disks barely move (conduction-dominated). The Plexiglas rods (k = 0.2 W/m/K) are treated as insulators.

Limits: Li in Al D = 4.5 e^(−139 kJ/mol/RT) cm²/s (Costas 1963) → 10 µm in a day at 327 °C; Li vapour pressure (CRC) → 1 µm gone in 10 h at 277 °C; LiF (ΔH_sub ≈ 256 kJ/mol, ESTIMATE) → 300 µg/cm² in a week at 477 °C. Li₂O melts at 1438 °C; LiOH at 462 °C.

target_model.py al_with_li(); nominal thin Li₂O/Li at 1.04–1.10 MeV: 0.6 %

8

Details

In 10 µm of Al a 1.04 MeV proton slows to ~0.48 MeV at the back face, so Li that has diffused deep sees energies just above the 441 keV resonance (Γ 12 keV, σ 50× the 1.03 MeV one). If the backing stops the beam, any diffused Li sees 441 keV exactly: ATOMKI 2016’s “actual target thickness = 10 µm” put most of their pairs on the 17.64 MeV M1 line.

Profile: half-Gaussian of width √(4Dt) from the film into the Al; the fraction diffused is a free parameter. LiF that loses fluorine under beam (Redigolo 2024 normalise to elastic scattering because CaF₂ loses F) frees Li that can do the same: 10–30 % freed → 0.8–1.1 % share.

scenarios.csv (group “diffusion”).

θ only

m_ee

θ × |y| × E_sum (MX17 reference)

hydration / carbon (open)

At a 20 % share the 3D fit reports -0.06 and its χ² rises by 891: the data reject the wrong target model.

The θ-only fit reports +0.20 with χ² ≈ 6: invisible. ATOMKI’s 6.8σ cannot come from this alone.

fit_bias.csv · reference: S_θ 2 % + S_θy 1 % structure; 30 days at 1 µA

9

Details

target_fit_bias.py: Δ = background(truth) − background(model) per day, from the same Geant4 events reweighted (lnl_nd.collect with the degraded target’s yields: γ₀/γ₁ totals, the 17.64 / 18.15 / direct split, the direct γ₁ share). The fitted parameter bias after T days is (TF + P)⁻¹ T b, as in the impostor test (FEASIBILITY_SIM §16). The fit floats M1, E1 and γ₁ norms, the γ* anisotropy, the θ resolution, the E_sum scale, the acceptance cubic, the |y| tilt, per-arm gains and the structure modes S_θ 2 % + S_θy 1 %. The θ-only and m_ee rows use the same nuisances in one variable.

“χ² left” is what the data still say after the fit has absorbed what it can: ≫ 1 means a 30-day run would see that the target model is wrong and could refit it (or fit the 441 share).

The 441 share is the knob for diffusion or a stopping backing (previous slide). Hydration: Li₂O fully converted to LiOH (×1.6 mass) or Li₂CO₃ (×2.47); carbon: 100 µg/cm² in front.

Left: γ₀ yield with carbon on the front, beam not retuned. Right: ¹¹B(p,γ₀) 16.9 MeV relative to ⁸Be γ₀ (estimate).

Fit (30 d): B/Li = 0.24 → fake r -0.019 in 3D (-0.029 θ only); B/Li = 10⁻² → -0.0008.

carbon.csv, scenarios.csv (boron rows), fit_bias.csv

10

Details

Carbon: 0.38 keV per µg/cm² at 441 keV, 0.22 keV at 1.07 MeV (PSTAR). On the 12 keV-wide 441 keV resonance a 30 µg/cm² LiF target loses 18 % of its yield for 10 µg/cm² of carbon; at 1.07 MeV the broad resonance makes it irrelevant. Build-up rates in the literature run from ~10¹⁴ C/cm²/µC to unmeasurable with a cold trap at 10⁻⁷ mbar (Redigolo 2024): use a cold trap and redo a short 441 keV scan per target.

Boron: ¹¹B(p,γ) has Q = 15.96 MeV, so γ₀ = 16.9 MeV at E_p ≈ 1.05 MeV, an E1 line between γ₁ (15 MeV) and γ₀ (18.15 MeV). σ(γ₀) ≈ 7.6 µb at 1.05 MeV (ESTIMATE, ×2), ¼ of ⁷Li(p,γ₀). Brine lithium carries up to ~500 ppm B before purification; BN crucibles are a common evaporation source. Fit (30 d): B/Li = 0.24 → fake r -0.019 in 3D (-0.029 θ only); B/Li = 10⁻² → -0.0008.

11

Details

Thin enough is easy: 100–300 µg/cm² is 0.5–1.5 µm of Li₂O, routine for evaporation (LiF was made to 184 µg/cm² with 6 % non-uniformity on a rotating substrate, arXiv:2208.03425). Known composition is the hard part, and it is measured with the beam itself, on the same machines.

Hydrogen: 2×10¹⁸ /cm² per day at 1 µA on a σ = 2 mm spot; Cu blisters somewhere between 10¹⁸ and 3×10¹⁹ /cm² (Budker/OIST at 2 MeV). With a 10 µm Al backing at 1.1 MeV the beam leaves the target and stops in the dump.

what this does not rule out, and what to ask

Not ruled out

• That LNL’s problem was elsewhere: acceptance drops near 140° (their own worry), cosmics (MEG II 2026), or statistics. The fluorine case is an inference from public facts.

• Their DAQ may have coped: the energy cuts remove single E0 pairs, and the problem is then rate and pile-up, which a toy cannot size better than ×2.

• Emissivity, spot size and LNL’s holder set the real temperature; the boron σ is an estimate (×2).

Ask LNL (Marchi, Góngora-Servín)

1. Trigger rate and dead time at 1.03 MeV vs 441 keV.

2. Backing, holder, spot; target lifetime and PIGE history.

3. α / proton absorber in front of the in-vacuum telescopes?

4. The thesis and the LDMA 2025 slides.

5. Target lab: Li₂O deposition, Ar transfer, B analysis.
